findings.desc: doc-promise-undelivered: packages/main/src/core/acceptance-discovery-adapters.ts:81 declares five registered discovery adapters, but buildResult assigns the same preassembled input.pathRefs to process_fact_registry, handler_dispatch_inventory, and static_call_graph, while runtime_trace performs no discovery. runAcceptanceDiscoveryAdapters only relabels this one input set; it never inspects handler/dispatch source, a static graph, or runtime facts. Because deriveAcceptanceCoverageBasis constructs input.pathRefs from the topology/planned declarations themselves, the adapters cannot independently discover an omitted path or naturally disagree and can falsely classify the self-described closure complete. This violates Wave 1A's independent registered-adapter exit condition.

packages/main/src/core/acceptance-coverage-basis.ts:160 computes closureFilesHash from only planned endpoint files; registered producer/consumer closure entries are appended as literal inventory strings and their referenced source files are never resolved or content-hashed. deriveRegisteredProcessFactClosure likewise emits producer/consumer labels rather than resolvable source paths (acceptance-discovery-adapters.ts:44). Therefore an out-of-scope registered consumer can change while closureFilesHash remains unchanged, defeating the receipt freshness binding explicitly required by Wave 1A.

packages/main/src/core/acceptance-coverage-basis.ts:278 contains the only topology-versus-basis and exclusion validation, but neither deriveAcceptanceCoverageBasis nor the production generate/read handlers call it (handlers/proofstory.ts:134-184,206-234). Worse, derivation seeds every topology path into expectedPathRefs at lines 194-203 and the echo adapters reproduce it, so an invented topology path can be absorbed into a complete signed basis. The smoke calls reconcileTopologyWithCoverageBasis directly, which does not prove the real acceptance_basis_generate/acceptance_basis path rejects the mutation.

packages/main/src/core/acceptance-coverage-basis.ts:289-291 implements exclusion eligibility as only a /^decision:/ string regex. It does not resolve the decisionRef from the canonical foundational decision store/schema, verify an eligible decision kind, or detect stale/unrelated decisions as required by CHK-004 and the plan. The smoke covers only free-form prose without a decision: prefix, so decision:anything would escape AT_UNJUSTIFIED_EXCLUSION. Add canonical decision resolution and negative tests for missing, stale, unrelated, and ineligible-kind refs (or explicitly leave all exclusions unsupported/non-complete in Wave 1A).

packages/main/src/core/acceptance-coverage-basis.ts:149-156 and :201-207 do not bind the discovered global closure source contents promised by closureFilesHash. computeClosureFilesHash hashes only files named by plannedPathRecords; sourceInventory entries for PROCESS_FACT_REGISTRY producers/consumer gates are merely hashed as identifier strings and are never resolved to source files. A consumer outside Story scope can change without its file content entering closureFilesHash, violating the explicit Wave 1A requirement that every discovered producer and consumer source reference, including outside storyFilesHash, be content-bound and uninspectable consumers force partial.

doc-promise-undelivered: packages/main/src/core/acceptance-coverage-basis.ts:194-204 and packages/main/src/core/acceptance-discovery-adapters.ts:81-108 do not implement independently derived discovery. deriveAcceptanceCoverageBasis first takes path refs from the submitted topology/planned declarations, then buildResult copies that same precomputed set verbatim into process_fact_registry, handler_dispatch_inventory, and static_call_graph while runtime_trace contributes nothing. Consequently deleting an undeclared real handler/dispatch/static consumer from topology makes every synthetic adapter agree and can still yield status=complete; there is no repository/handler/dispatch/static/runtime inspection. This contradicts the Wave 1A exit condition and the new CLI promise that the registered profile derives the union. Implement method-specific adapters from canonical repository/runtime inputs and prove an actual omitted consumer is discovered/fails closed.

CHK-001 must coverage is overclaimed: packages/main/src/tasks/proofstory-acceptance-basis-smoke.ts:235 exercises only status/enumeratedPathRefs/issuer on the read command. VI-A32A-001-CALLER-FORGERY explicitly requires every public entry point and status, enumeratedPathRefs, blindSpots, excludedPathRefs, generatedBy, and digest fields, including the direct handler boundary. No assertions cover the remaining fields, acceptance_basis_generate, or direct-handler rejection/ignore semantics, so its recorded manual_transcript is not sufficient.
